title: Your Sofa, Week Three
subject: a man sleeping on his friend's sofa for a third week after a flat fell through, folding the duvet into a perfect square by seven every morning and learning to dodge the friend's cat at the fridge
caption: Electro swing, Parov Stelar and Caravan Palace style. Muted trumpet riffs, walking upright bass, swung hi-hat over a four-on-the-floor house kick, ragtime piano stabs, quick clarinet runs. Crackly gramophone-filtered horns over a clean modern house low end. Male tenor, clearly sung crooner melody with a wink. 124 BPM, G minor. Wry, bouncy, grateful. No trap, no autotune, no dubstep wobble, no rapped verses, no heavy distortion.
lyrics:
[Intro - gramophone horns, house kick]

[Verse 1]
The duvet's folded in a square
By seven on the dot
My socks are in a carrier bag
My toothbrush in a pot

[Pre-Chorus]
You said a weekend, maybe two
The cat is not convinced

[Chorus]
Your sofa, week three
I know every spring by name
I owe you dinners, two or three
And the cushion's never been the same

[Verse 2]
The cat waits by the fridge at six
And stares me down for ham
I tiptoe past your bedroom door
With toast and someone's jam

[Pre-Chorus]
The letting agent rang today
I nearly kissed the phone

[Chorus]
Your sofa, week three
I know every spring by name
On Friday I'll give back your key
But I'll miss the cat all the same

[Outro - muted trumpet tag]
